USD|Housing Starts.notes: While this is monthly data, it's reported in an annualized format (monthly figure x12). This data is slightly overshadowed by Building Permits because they are tightly correlated and a permit must be issued before a house can begin construction
USD|Housing Starts.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency

USD|ISM Manufacturing PMI.measures: Level of a diffusion index based on surveyed purchasing managers in the manufacturing industry
USD|ISM Manufacturing PMI.notes: Above 50.0 indicates industry expansion, below indicates contraction
USD|ISM Manufacturing PMI.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|ISM Manufacturing PMI.why: It's a leading indicator of economic health - businesses react quickly to market conditions, and their purchasing managers hold perhaps the most current and relevant insight into the company's view of the economy

USD|ISM Manufacturing Prices.measures: Level of a diffusion index based on surveyed purchasing managers in the manufacturing industry
USD|ISM Manufacturing Prices.notes: This is a component of PMI but reported separately as an inflation gauge. Above 50.0 indicates rising prices, below indicates falling prices
USD|ISM Manufacturing Prices.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|ISM Manufacturing Prices.why: It's a leading indicator of consumer inflation - when businesses pay more for goods and services the higher costs are usually passed on to the consumer

USD|ISM Services PMI.measures: Level of a diffusion index based on surveyed purchasing managers, excluding the manufacturing industry
USD|ISM Services PMI.notes: Above 50.0 indicates industry expansion, below indicates contraction. Source changed series from unadjusted to seasonally adjusted as of January 2001. Source changed series calculation formula as of Feb 2008
USD|ISM Services PMI.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|ISM Services PMI.why: It's a leading indicator of economic health - businesses react quickly to market conditions, and their purchasing managers hold perhaps the most current and relevant insight into the company's view of the economy

USD|Import Prices m/m.measures: Change in the price of imported goods and services purchased domestically
USD|Import Prices m/m.notes: This is the earliest government-released inflation data
USD|Import Prices m/m.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Import Prices m/m.why: It contributes to inflation for businesses and consumers, especially those who rely heavily on imported goods and services

USD|Industrial Production m/m.measures: Change in the total inflation-adjusted value of output produced by manufacturers, mines, and utilities
USD|Industrial Production m/m.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Industrial Production m/m.why: It's a leading indicator of economic health - production reacts quickly to ups and downs in the business cycle and is correlated with consumer conditions such as employment levels and earnings

USD|JOLTS Job Openings.measures: Number of job openings during the reported month, excluding the farming industry
USD|JOLTS Job Openings.notes: It's released late, but can impact the market because job openings are a leading indicator of overall employment
USD|JOLTS Job Openings.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|JOLTS Job Openings.why: Job creation is an important leading indicator of consumer spending, which accounts for a majority of overall economic activity

USD|Labor Market Conditions Index m/m.measures: Change in the level of a composite index based on 19 labor market indicators
USD|Labor Market Conditions Index m/m.notes: Source discontinued this data in Jul 2017
USD|Labor Market Conditions Index m/m.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency

USD|Loan Officer Survey.notes: Source does not have a reliable release schedule - this event will be listed with a date range or as 'Tentative' until the data is released
USD|Loan Officer Survey.why: It's correlated with spending and confidence - rising debt levels are a sign that lenders feel comfortable issuing loans, and that consumers and businesses are confident in their financial position and eager to spend money

USD|Mortgage Delinquencies.measures: Percentage of MBA-represented mortgages which were at least one payment late during the previous quarter
USD|Mortgage Delinquencies.notes: MBA represents about 80% of all outstanding mortgages. Source does not have a reliable release schedule - this event will be listed with a date range or as 'Tentative' until the data is released
USD|Mortgage Delinquencies.usual_effect: 'Actual' less than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Mortgage Delinquencies.why: Although it's generally viewed as a lagging indicator, the number of delinquencies can be an important signal of the housing market's health because it's correlated with home inventories. Lower inventories will spur homebuilders to start new construction

USD|NAHB Housing Market Index.measures: Level of a diffusion index based on surveyed home builders
USD|NAHB Housing Market Index.notes: Above 50 indicates a favorable outlook on home sales, below indicates a negative outlook
USD|NAHB Housing Market Index.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency

USD|NFIB Small Business Index.measures: Level of a composite index based on surveyed small businesses
USD|NFIB Small Business Index.notes: Small Businesses are defined as an independent for-profit enterprise that employ between 1 and 250 people, not including the owners
USD|NFIB Small Business Index.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency

USD|Natural Gas Storage.measures: Change in the number of cubic feet of natural gas held in underground storage during the past week
USD|Natural Gas Storage.notes: Inventories are used to maintain price stability during supply shortages and periods of increasing demand
USD|Natural Gas Storage.usual_effect: 'Actual' less than 'Forecast' is good for currency

USD|New Home Sales.measures: Annualized number of new single-family homes that were sold during the previous month
USD|New Home Sales.notes: While this is monthly data, it's reported in an annualized format (monthly figure x12)
USD|New Home Sales.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|New Home Sales.why: It's a leading indicator of economic health because the sale of a new home triggers a wide-reaching ripple effect. For example, furniture and appliances are purchased for the home, a mortgage is sold by the financing bank, and brokers are paid to execute the transaction

USD|Non-Farm Employment Change.measures: Change in the number of employed people during the previous month, excluding the farming industry
USD|Non-Farm Employment Change.notes: This is vital economic data released shortly after the month ends. The combination of importance and earliness makes for hefty market impacts
USD|Non-Farm Employment Change.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Non-Farm Employment Change.why: Job creation is an important leading indicator of consumer spending, which accounts for a majority of overall economic activity

USD|PPI m/m.measures: Change in the price of finished goods and services sold by producers
USD|PPI m/m.notes: Source changed series calculation formula as of Feb 2014
USD|PPI m/m.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|PPI m/m.why: It's a leading indicator of consumer inflation - when producers charge more for goods and services the higher costs are usually passed on to the consumer

USD|Pending Home Sales m/m.measures: Change in the number of homes under contract to be sold but still awaiting the closing transaction, excluding new construction
USD|Pending Home Sales m/m.notes: This data is released about a week later than Existing Home Sales, but it's more forward-looking as a contract is signed several weeks before the home is counted as sold
USD|Pending Home Sales m/m.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Pending Home Sales m/m.why: It's a leading indicator of economic health because the sale of a home triggers a wide-reaching ripple effect. For example, renovations are done by the new owners, a mortgage is sold by the financing bank, and brokers are paid to execute the transaction

USD|Personal Income m/m.measures: Change in the total value of income received from all sources by consumers
USD|Personal Income m/m.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Personal Income m/m.why: Income is correlated with spending - the more disposable income consumers have, the more likely they are to increase spending

USD|Personal Spending m/m.measures: Change in the inflation-adjusted value of all expenditures by consumers
USD|Personal Spending m/m.notes: This is significant data, though it tends to have a relatively mild impact because Retail Sales, which also covers consumer spending, is released about 2 weeks earlier
USD|Personal Spending m/m.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Personal Spending m/m.why: Consumer spending accounts for a majority of overall economic activity. It's one of the most important gauges of economic health due to the vast ripple effect consumer buying creates in the economy

USD|Philly Fed Manufacturing Index.measures: Level of a diffusion index based on surveyed manufacturers in Philadelphia
USD|Philly Fed Manufacturing Index.notes: Above 0.0 indicates improving conditions, below indicates worsening conditions
USD|Philly Fed Manufacturing Index.source: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia (latest release)
USD|Philly Fed Manufacturing Index.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Philly Fed Manufacturing Index.why: It's a leading indicator of economic health - businesses react quickly to market conditions, and changes in their sentiment can be an early signal of future economic activity such as spending, hiring, and investment

USD|Prelim GDP Price Index q/q.measures: Annualized change in the price of all goods and services included in GDP
USD|Prelim GDP Price Index q/q.notes: While this is q/q data, it's reported in an annualized format (quarterly change x4). The 'Previous' listed is the 'Actual' from the Advance release and therefore the 'History' data will appear unconnected
USD|Prelim GDP Price Index q/q.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency

USD|Prelim GDP q/q.measures: Annualized change in the value of all goods and services produced by the economy
USD|Prelim GDP q/q.notes: While this is q/q data, it's reported in an annualized format (quarterly change x4). The 'Previous' listed is the 'Actual' from the Advance release and therefore the 'History' data will appear unconnected. There are 3 versions of GDP released a month apart - Advance, Preliminary, and Final. The Advance release is the earliest and thus tends to have the most impact
USD|Prelim GDP q/q.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Prelim GDP q/q.why: It's the broadest measure of economic activity and the primary gauge of the economy's health

USD|Prelim Nonfarm Productivity q/q.measures: Annualized change in labor efficiency when producing goods and services, excluding the farming industry
USD|Prelim Nonfarm Productivity q/q.notes: While this is q/q data, it's reported in an annualized format (quarterly change x4). Due to the double revision schedule the 'History' data will appear unconnected. There are 2 versions of this report released a month apart – Preliminary and Revised. The Preliminary release is the earliest and thus tends to have the most impact
USD|Prelim Nonfarm Productivity q/q.usual_effect: 'Actual' less than 'Forecast' is good for currency

USD|Prelim Unit Labor Costs q/q.measures: Annualized change in the price businesses pay for labor, excluding the farming industry
USD|Prelim Unit Labor Costs q/q.notes: While this is q/q data, it's reported in an annualized format (quarterly change x4). Due to the double revision schedule the 'History' data will appear unconnected. There are 2 versions of this report released a month apart – Preliminary and Revised. The Preliminary release is the earliest and thus tends to have the most impact
USD|Prelim Unit Labor Costs q/q.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency

USD|Prelim UoM Consumer Sentiment.measures: Level of a composite index based on surveyed consumers
USD|Prelim UoM Consumer Sentiment.notes: There are 2 versions of this data released 14 days apart – Preliminary and Revised. The Preliminary release is the earlier and thus tends to have the most impact
USD|Prelim UoM Consumer Sentiment.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Prelim UoM Consumer Sentiment.why: Financial confidence is a leading indicator of consumer spending, which accounts for a majority of overall economic activity

USD|Prelim UoM Inflation Expectations.measures: Percentage that consumers expect the price of goods and services to change during the next 12 months
USD|Prelim UoM Inflation Expectations.notes: There are 2 versions of this data released 14 days apart – Preliminary and Revised. The Preliminary release is the earlier and thus tends to have the most impact
USD|Prelim UoM Inflation Expectations.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Prelim UoM Inflation Expectations.why: Expectations of future inflation can manifest into real inflation, primarily because workers tend to push for higher wages when they believe prices will rise

USD|Prelim Wholesale Inventories m/m.measures: Change in the total value of goods held in inventory by wholesalers
USD|Prelim Wholesale Inventories m/m.notes: There are 2 versions of this report released about a week apart – Preliminary and Final. The Preliminary release, which the source first reported in Aug 2016, is the earliest and thus tends to have the most impact.
USD|Prelim Wholesale Inventories m/m.usual_effect: 'Actual' less than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Prelim Wholesale Inventories m/m.why: It's a signal of future business spending because companies are more likely to purchase goods once they have depleted inventories

USD|RCM/TIPP Economic Optimism.measures: Level of a diffusion index based on surveyed consumers
USD|RCM/TIPP Economic Optimism.notes: Above 50.0 indicates optimism, below indicates pessimism. Source does not give an exact release time - this event will be listed as 'Tentative' until the data is released
USD|RCM/TIPP Economic Optimism.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency

USD|Retail Sales m/m.measures: Change in the total value of sales at the retail level
USD|Retail Sales m/m.notes: This is the earliest and broadest look at vital consumer spending data
USD|Retail Sales m/m.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Retail Sales m/m.why: It's the primary gauge of consumer spending, which accounts for the majority of overall economic activity

USD|Revised Nonfarm Productivity q/q.measures: Annualized change in labor efficiency when producing goods and services, excluding the farming industry

USD|Revised Unit Labor Costs q/q.measures: Annualized change in the price businesses pay for labor, excluding the farming industry
USD|Revised Unit Labor Costs q/q.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency

USD|Revised UoM Consumer Sentiment.measures: Level of a composite index based on surveyed consumers
USD|Revised UoM Consumer Sentiment.notes: The 'Previous' listed is the 'Actual' from the Preliminary release and therefore the 'History' data will appear unconnected. There are 2 versions of this data released about 15 days apart – Preliminary and Revised. The Preliminary release is the earliest and thus tends to have more impact
USD|Revised UoM Consumer Sentiment.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Revised UoM Consumer Sentiment.why: Financial confidence is a leading indicator of consumer spending, which accounts for a majority of overall economic activity

USD|Revised UoM Inflation Expectations.measures: Percentage that consumers expect the price of goods and services to change during the next 12 months
USD|Revised UoM Inflation Expectations.notes: The 'Previous' listed is the 'Actual' from the Preliminary release and therefore the 'History' data will appear unconnected. There are 2 versions of this data released about 15 days apart – Preliminary and Revised. The Preliminary release is the earliest and thus tends to have more impact
USD|Revised UoM Inflation Expectations.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Revised UoM Inflation Expectations.why: Expectations of future inflation can manifest into real inflation, primarily because workers tend to push for higher wages when they believe prices will rise

USD|Richmond Manufacturing Index.measures: Level of a composite index based on surveyed manufacturers in Richmond
USD|Richmond Manufacturing Index.notes: Above 0 indicates improving conditions, below indicates worsening conditions. Tends to have a muted impact because there are earlier regional indicators related to manufacturing conditions
USD|Richmond Manufacturing Index.source: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond (latest release)
USD|Richmond Manufacturing Index.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency

USD|S&P/CS Composite-20 HPI y/y.measures: Change in the selling price of single-family homes in 20 metropolitan areas
USD|S&P/CS Composite-20 HPI y/y.notes: This is one of the few non-seasonally adjusted numbers reported on the calendar, as it's the primary calculation for this indicator
USD|S&P/CS Composite-20 HPI y/y.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|S&P/CS Composite-20 HPI y/y.why: It's a leading indicator of the housing industry's health because rising house prices attract investors and spur industry activity

USD|TIC Long-Term Purchases.measures: Difference in value between foreign long-term securities purchased by US citizens and US long-term securities purchased by foreigners during the reported period
USD|TIC Long-Term Purchases.notes: This data represents the balance of domestic and foreign investment - for example, if foreigners purchased $100 billion in US stocks and bonds, and the US purchased $30 billion in foreign stocks and bonds, the net reading would be 70.0B
USD|TIC Long-Term Purchases.source: US Department of the Treasury (latest release)
USD|TIC Long-Term Purchases.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|TIC Long-Term Purchases.why: Demand for domestic securities and currency demand are directly linked because foreigners must buy the domestic currency to purchase the nation's securities

USD|Total Vehicle Sales.measures: Annualized number of cars and trucks sold domestically during the previous month
USD|Total Vehicle Sales.notes: Source discontinued this data in Apr 2019
USD|Total Vehicle Sales.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Total Vehicle Sales.why: It's a sign of consumer confidence - rising demand for expensive durable goods shows that consumers are confident in their future financial position and feel comfortable spending money

USD|Trade Balance.measures: Difference in value between imported and exported goods and services during the reported month
USD|Trade Balance.notes: The goods portion has a muted impact because it's a duplicate of the Goods Trade Balance data released about 5 days earlier. A positive number indicates that more goods and services were exported than imported
USD|Trade Balance.usual_effect: 'Actual' greater than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Trade Balance.why: Export demand and currency demand are directly linked because foreigners must buy the domestic currency to pay for the nation's exports. Export demand also impacts production and prices at domestic manufacturers

USD|Treasury Currency Report.notes: Source does not provide a reliable release time and the report can be delayed for several days - the event will be listed as 'Tentative' until the report is issued. Market impact tends to vary and is mostly dependent on which countries the report will accuse of currency manipulation
USD|Treasury Currency Report.source: US Department of the Treasury (latest release)
USD|Treasury Currency Report.why: It provides a detailed review of global exchange rate policies, economic conditions, and central bank and government actions around the world. Most importantly, the report outlines countries that the Treasury deems currency manipulators

USD|Treasury Sec Lew Speaks.notes: US Treasury Secretary Feb 2013 - Jan 2017. He speaks frequently on a broad range of subjects - only speeches that might have direct market impact are listed on the calendar

USD|Treasury Sec Mnuchin Speaks.notes: US Treasury Secretary Feb 2017 - Jan 2021. He speaks frequently on a broad range of subjects - only speeches that might have direct market impact are listed on the calendar

USD|Treasury Sec Paulson Speaks.notes: US Treasury Secretary Jul 2006 - Jan 2009. He speaks frequently on a broad range of subjects - only speeches that might have direct market impact are listed on the calendar
USD|Treasury Sec Paulson Speaks.source: US Department of the Treasury (latest release)
USD|Treasury Sec Paulson Speaks.why: It's the Treasury Secretary's job to communicate the US President's economic policies, and his speeches are often used to signal policy shifts to the public and to foreign governments

USD|Treasury Sec Yellen Speaks.source: US Department of the Treasury (latest release)

USD|Unemployment Claims.measures: The number of individuals who filed for unemployment insurance for the first time during the past week
USD|Unemployment Claims.notes: This is the nation's earliest economic data. The market impact fluctuates from week to week - there tends to be more focus on the release when traders need to diagnose recent developments, or when the reading is at extremes
USD|Unemployment Claims.usual_effect: 'Actual' less than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Unemployment Claims.why: Although it's generally viewed as a lagging indicator, the number of unemployed people is an important signal of overall economic health because consumer spending is highly correlated with labor-market conditions. Unemployment is also a major consideration for those steering the country's monetary policy

USD|Unemployment Rate.measures: Percentage of the total work force that is unemployed and actively seeking employment during the previous month
USD|Unemployment Rate.usual_effect: 'Actual' less than 'Forecast' is good for currency
USD|Unemployment Rate.why: Although it's generally viewed as a lagging indicator, the number of unemployed people is an important signal of overall economic health because consumer spending is highly correlated with labor-market conditions. Unemployment is also a major consideration for those steering the country's monetary policy
